chunks: ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, from Khālid ibn Najīḥ, from Zurārah ibn Aʿyan, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “The boy must inevitably have a ghaybah (occultation).”

I said, “And why?” He عليه السلام said: “He will fear,” and he gestured with his hand toward his belly. “And he is al-Muntaẓar, and he is the one concerning whose birth people will doubt. So among them are those who will say: ‘A pregnancy’; and among them are those who will say: ‘His father died and left no successor’; and among them are those who will say: ‘He was born two years before his father’s death.’”
Zurārah said: So I said, “What do you command me to do if I reach that time?” He عليه السلام said: “Supplicate to Allah with this duʿāʾ:”

O Allah, make me know Yourself, for if You do not make me know Yourself, I will not know You. O Allah, make me know Your Prophet, for if You do not make me know Your Prophet, I will never know him. O Allah, make me know Your Ḥujjah, for if You do not make me know Your Ḥujjah, I will go astray from my religion.
Aḥmad ibn al-Hilāl said: “I heard this hadith fifty-six years ago.”

key_terms.ادْعُ: supplicate; invoke Allah with the taught prayer
key_terms.الْغُلَامِ: the boy; a reference to the awaited Imam
key_terms.حُجَّتَكَ: Your divine proof; Allah’s authoritative representative
key_terms.دِينِي: my religion, from which one may stray without right recognition
key_terms.غَيْبَةٍ: occultation; a period of concealed presence
key_terms.نَبِيَّكَ: Your Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.وِلَادَتِهِ: his birth, about which people will dispute

ai.seo_question: What duʿāʾ did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام teach for remaining guided during the ghaybah?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the promised boy will necessarily enter ghaybah (occultation), and that people will differ and doubt the circumstances of his birth and succession. It also teaches a foundational duʿāʾ for times of confusion, asking Allah to grant recognition of Himself, His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and His Ḥujjah so that one does not go astray from the religion.
